decisions.title: Closed ECMAScript edition
decisions.issue: The live draft and Test262 gain syntax and semantics after each published edition, so an unpinned implementation can change behavior without a package release decision.
interpretations: Accept every Test262 feature understood by the parser.
Close syntax and semantics to one published edition.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained JavaScript engines ship proposals and corrections on different schedules; their current acceptance does not redefine a published edition.
decisions.selected_behavior: The package implements exactly ECMA-262 16th edition and rejects or excludes later proposal and live-draft behavior until an explicit edition upgrade.
decisions.rationale: A closed edition makes accepted grammar and semantics reproducible and compatibility-reviewable.
decisions.security_consequences: Unreviewed syntax cannot create new parser or execution states.
decisions.resource_consequences: Existing finite parse, compile, and execution limits remain the complete resource contract.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Pattern and flag acceptance stays stable until a reviewed edition upgrade.
decisions.wire_consequences: Patterns carry no edition negotiation field, so callers must coordinate edition upgrades.
decisions.upstream_status: The publication, source commit, Test262 feature inventory, and draft audit boundary are pinned in repository evidence.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later published ECMA-262 edition is selected and its complete grammar and semantic delta has executable evidence.

decisions.title: Pattern engine rather than JavaScript RegExp object model
decisions.issue: ECMA-262 combines Pattern semantics with JavaScript constructors, prototypes, coercion, descriptors, species, and RegExp.escape that a native Go API does not expose.
interpretations: Emulate the complete JavaScript object model.
Implement overlapping Pattern and matcher semantics and account for excluded host-object tests.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines expose the complete object model, while maintained native regexp libraries overlap only on pattern compilation and matching.
decisions.selected_behavior: The package implements Pattern grammar, matching, captures, indices, state, replacement, and split through typed Go APIs; JavaScript host-object behavior is out of scope and explicitly accounted.
decisions.rationale: The boundary provides native deterministic semantics without claiming absent host-language behavior.
decisions.security_consequences: No production path evaluates JavaScript or invokes implicit host callbacks.
decisions.resource_consequences: Native parsing and matching remain bounded by caller-visible limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Semantic pattern results can be compared with peers, but JavaScript object identity and coercion are not supported.
decisions.wire_consequences: Results are typed Go values rather than serialized JavaScript objects.
decisions.upstream_status: Every pinned Test262 RegExp file is classified by applicable behavior instead of being silently omitted.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separately versioned package intentionally implements JavaScript RegExp host objects.

decisions.title: UTF-16 indices with explicit Go mappings
decisions.issue: ECMAScript indices count UTF-16 code units while Go strings are byte sequences and Go callers also need rune coordinates.
interpretations: Make UTF-16 normative and expose derived byte and rune mappings.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines report UTF-16 indices; Go regexp libraries report byte offsets.
decisions.selected_behavior: Match and capture indices are normatively UTF-16 code-unit offsets, with byte and rune mappings for Go-string inputs and exact unit offsets for UTF-16 inputs.
decisions.rationale: The result preserves ECMAScript semantics without discarding Go interoperability metadata.
decisions.security_consequences: Explicit validated mappings prevent slicing at invalid boundaries.
decisions.resource_consequences: Mappings are computed once within input limits and use bounded integer conversions.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must select the coordinate system named by the API instead of assuming Go byte offsets.
decisions.wire_consequences: Serialized indices must identify UTF-16 units; byte and rune offsets are additional Go metadata.
decisions.upstream_status: ECMA-262 algorithms operate over UTF-16 code units; Go coordinate mappings are an explicit package extension.
decisions.reconsider_when: ECMA-262 changes its string model or another input representation is added.

decisions.title: Invalid UTF-8 in Go strings
decisions.issue: ECMAScript strings are UTF-16 sequences but Go strings may contain invalid UTF-8 bytes that have no direct ECMAScript scalar interpretation.
interpretations: Preserve each invalid byte as an invented surrogate.
Decode each invalid byte as U+FFFD while retaining source byte offsets.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript string APIs cannot receive arbitrary invalid UTF-8 bytes; Go iteration decodes each invalid byte as U+FFFD.
decisions.selected_behavior: Each invalid Go-string byte maps to one U+FFFD code point and retains its original byte boundary; exact surrogate input uses the UTF-16 APIs.
decisions.rationale: The policy follows Go decoding and remains deterministic without inventing ECMAScript code units.
decisions.security_consequences: Invalid bytes cannot bypass matching through inconsistent decoders.
decisions.resource_consequences: Each input byte contributes at most one bounded mapping entry.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Invalid UTF-8 matches replacement-character behavior and may differ from byte-oriented regexp engines.
decisions.wire_consequences: Exact invalid bytes are not preserved through Unicode string serialization; byte offsets still identify the source.
decisions.upstream_status: ECMA-262 does not define conversion from invalid Go UTF-8; this is package policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A byte-oriented input API or a different explicit invalid-input profile is introduced.

decisions.title: Pinned Unicode data and exact aliases
decisions.section: UCD 16.0.0 and ECMA-262 Unicode property escape algorithms
decisions.issue: Unicode data evolves independently from ECMA-262 and host runtimes, while loose property aliases would accept spellings ECMAScript requires to match exactly.
interpretations: Use the Go toolchain Unicode tables.
Fetch current Unicode data at build time.
Generate immutable tables from one digest-pinned Unicode release and apply exact aliases.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines and Go releases ship different Unicode versions; maintained engine disagreement can therefore be version-specific.
decisions.selected_behavior: The package uses generated Unicode 16.0.0 properties, case folding, identifiers, emoji sequences, and properties of strings with exact ECMAScript aliases.
decisions.rationale: Pinned generated tables make behavior reproducible across hosts and releases.
decisions.security_consequences: Digest verification prevents silent corpus substitution and exact aliases avoid confusable spellings.
decisions.resource_consequences: Generated immutable tables avoid runtime network access and keep lookup bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Newer Unicode characters retain the 16.0.0 result until an explicit data upgrade.
decisions.wire_consequences: Pattern property names and matches are stable for the pinned Unicode release.
decisions.upstream_status: UCD, emoji sequence, and emoji ZWJ inputs are independently digest-pinned and their release index is monitored.
decisions.reconsider_when: A reviewed package release selects a different Unicode version.

decisions.title: Unicode modes, Unicode Sets, and Annex B
decisions.section: Pattern grammar, UnicodeMode, Unicode Sets, and Annex B.1.4
decisions.issue: Legacy, u, and v grammars differ materially, u and v conflict, and Annex B extends only legacy web grammar.
interpretations: Select the exact grammar from validated flags and explicit legacy policy.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained JavaScript engines select grammar from flags and implement Annex B in non-Unicode mode.
decisions.selected_behavior: Flags are closed to d g i m s u v y; u and v conflict; u selects Unicode grammar, v selects Unicode Sets grammar, and Annex B is available only through explicit legacy policy.
decisions.rationale: Mode-specific grammar prevents legacy compatibility syntax from weakening Unicode early errors.
decisions.security_consequences: Closed modes prevent ambiguous parser states and unreviewed syntax.
decisions.resource_consequences: Each selected grammar remains subject to the same finite parse and compile budgets.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Patterns accepted only by a permissive union parser are rejected in their actual mode.
decisions.wire_consequences: Pattern text has meaning only with its exact validated flags and legacy policy.
decisions.upstream_status: The pinned edition and feature register define each applicable grammar and proposal boundary.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later edition changes grammar modes, flags, or Annex B applicability.

decisions.title: Duplicate named captures in disjoint alternatives
decisions.section: Pattern early errors for duplicate GroupName
decisions.issue: Edition 16 permits duplicate names only when alternatives prove that at most one same-named capture can participate.
interpretations: Accept all duplicate names and choose a capture dynamically.
decisions.peer_behavior: Current JavaScript engines adopted the edition-specific relaxation on different schedules.
decisions.selected_behavior: Duplicate named captures are accepted only when static alternative analysis proves they cannot both participate; resolution uses the participating capture.
decisions.rationale: This implements the edition rule without introducing ambiguous capture ownership.
decisions.security_consequences: Static proof avoids attacker-controlled ambiguity in replacement and backreference resolution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Disjointness analysis is bounded by AST limits and does not execute the pattern.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Older engines may reject valid edition-16 patterns and permissive engines may accept patterns rejected here.
decisions.wire_consequences: Named capture maps contain one logical name and the participating capture value.
decisions.upstream_status: The pinned edition and Test262 duplicate-name fixtures define the accepted boundary.
decisions.reconsider_when: ECMA-262 changes duplicate-name early errors or capture resolution.

decisions.title: Zero-width progress and stateful lastIndex
decisions.issue: Stateful execution exposes UTF-16 lastIndex, while repeated collection operations must progress after empty matches without splitting Unicode code points.
interpretations: Advance by the selected Unicode mode while keeping lastIndex in UTF-16 units.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines expose UTF-16 lastIndex and mode-aware AdvanceStringIndex behavior.
decisions.selected_behavior: Session lastIndex is UTF-16; global and sticky failure resets it as specified; collection operations advance empty matches by one code unit or one Unicode code point according to mode.
decisions.rationale: The state contract remains ECMAScript-compatible while every repeated operation terminates.
decisions.security_consequences: Empty matches cannot create infinite loops.
decisions.resource_consequences: Progress is monotonic and result limits bound collection growth.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers observe UTF-16 state rather than Go byte offsets and deterministic empty-match progression.
decisions.wire_consequences: Persisted session indices must be interpreted as UTF-16 code units.
decisions.upstream_status: ECMA-262 defines stateful execution; package collection APIs apply the same progress rule explicitly.
decisions.reconsider_when: The supported edition changes lastIndex or AdvanceStringIndex semantics.

decisions.title: JSON Schema pattern profile
decisions.issue: JSON Schema recommends ECMA-262-compatible regular expressions but carries pattern text without JavaScript flags and requires substring rather than implicit whole-string matching.
interpretations: Use a closed Unicode ECMAScript profile with unanchored search semantics.
decisions.peer_behavior: JSON Schema validators vary between ECMA-262, PCRE, RE2, and documented portable subsets.
decisions.selected_behavior: CompileJSONSchemaPattern selects ECMAScript Unicode u semantics, performs unanchored search unless the pattern supplies anchors, exposes no hidden caller flags, and propagates ordinary limits.
decisions.rationale: The profile follows Draft 2020-12 guidance while making the otherwise absent flag selection explicit.
decisions.security_consequences: The same parse and execution budgets apply to schema-controlled patterns and instance strings.
decisions.resource_consequences: Schema matching is synchronous and bounded with no remote loading.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: RE2-, PCRE-, or legacy-mode validators can accept or reject different patterns; portability guidance documents the subset.
decisions.wire_consequences: Pattern remains ordinary JSON Schema text with no added flag field.
decisions.upstream_status: Draft 2020-12 validation guidance recommends ECMA-262 regular expressions but does not define a JavaScript flag transport.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later JSON Schema dialect changes its regular-expression requirement or adds explicit mode negotiation.

decisions.title: Bounded native execution and cancellation
decisions.section: Pattern evaluation algorithms and host-defined resource policy
decisions.issue: ECMA-262 specifies results but does not select finite native parser, compiler, backtracking, recursion, output, cancellation, or wall-time budgets.
interpretations: Use hidden worker goroutines and abandon timed-out work.
Preserve semantics within explicit synchronous budgets and classified failures.
decisions.peer_behavior: Maintained engines and regexp libraries apply different hidden or configurable resource policies.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parsing, compilation, matching, backtracking, recursion, allocation, results, output, cancellation, and wall time have explicit finite synchronous limits and typed errors; no hidden worker survives return.
decisions.rationale: Callers retain ownership of resource policy without weakening supported ECMAScript semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Hostile patterns cannot consume unbounded CPU, memory, stack, goroutines, or output.
decisions.resource_consequences: Every untrusted-size and execution dimension is checked before unbounded work or allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Valid patterns can return limit or cancellation errors under configured budgets instead of producing a match result.
decisions.wire_consequences: Limit failures are typed local errors and never partial serialized results.
decisions.upstream_status: The resource policy is defensive package behavior and is not presented as an ECMA-262 requirement.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new execution backend or public operation adds a resource dimension not covered by the current limits.

decisions.title: Test262 applicability and negative syntax accounting
decisions.issue: Test262 files mix Pattern grammar, JavaScript source tokenization, matcher calls, host-object behavior, proposals, and harness semantics, so raw pass counts overstate native pattern conformance.
interpretations: Run convenient fixtures without a denominator.
Inventory every pinned file and classify the exact behavior executed.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines use the official harness and naturally cover host objects; native libraries require scoped adapters.
decisions.selected_behavior: Every pinned RegExp and RegExp-literal file is classified as matcher, generated structural, syntax, lexical-only, proposal-stage, host-object-only, or outside the public surface; only exercised behavior is claimed.
decisions.rationale: Attributable accounting prevents unsupported JavaScript APIs from inflating conformance claims.
decisions.security_consequences: Corpus provisioning is digest-pinned and tests execute without fixture-controlled network or file access.
decisions.resource_consequences: Corpus runs use disposable storage and the engine limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Published counts describe applicable behavior rather than an incomparable percentage of the JavaScript object model.
decisions.wire_consequences: Fixture classifications are evidence metadata and do not change runtime results.
decisions.upstream_status: The Test262 commit and license digest are pinned; feature and file accounting changes require review.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Test262 pin, public surface, or harness classification changes.

decisions.title: Differential engines and classified divergence
decisions.section: Maintained-peer comparison policy for applicable RegExp semantics
decisions.issue: One runtime can share a bug, proposal state, or Unicode version with this package, while peer disagreement is evidence rather than a normative vote.
interpretations: Compare equivalent semantics across maintained independent engine families and classify each divergence.
decisions.peer_behavior: Pinned Node.js and Deno use V8, Bun uses JavaScriptCore, regexp2 is a maintained native engine, and goja is a maintained Go JavaScript runtime.
decisions.selected_behavior: The release differential compares pattern, flags, input, match, captures, and UTF-16 indices across at least two independent engine families plus maintained Go peers where semantics overlap; every disagreement is minimized and classified.
decisions.rationale: Independent implementations expose local, peer, fixture, harness, ambiguity, and deliberate-policy defects without replacing normative source review.
decisions.security_consequences: Differential subprocesses are test-only, pinned, time-bounded, and receive generated non-secret vectors.
decisions.resource_consequences: The fixed vector inventory and test timeouts bound subprocess and in-process comparisons.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Peer-version differences remain visible and never silently redefine the supported edition.
decisions.wire_consequences: Semantic fields are compared while irrelevant host serializer formatting is excluded.
decisions.upstream_status: Runtime families, exact versions, vector counts, and the one reviewed JavaScriptCore divergence are retained in the differential register.
decisions.reconsider_when: A peer becomes unmaintained, changes engine family, or a normative correction resolves a recorded divergence.

decisions.title: Replacement and split on exact UTF-16 input
decisions.issue: Replacement tokens, unmatched captures, empty matches, surrogate pairs, and lone surrogates expose incompatible Go byte and ECMAScript UTF-16 slicing behavior.
interpretations: Convert every input to Unicode scalars.
Preserve exact UTF-16 units and implement ECMAScript substitution parsing.
decisions.peer_behavior: JavaScript engines preserve UTF-16 code units and implement ECMAScript substitution tokens; Go string helpers do neither.
decisions.selected_behavior: Replacement and split implement ECMAScript substitution and capture insertion over exact UTF-16 boundaries; UTF-16 APIs preserve lone surrogates and Go-string APIs preserve original byte slices through explicit mappings.
decisions.rationale: Exact boundaries prevent data corruption while matching the supported edition token semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Token parsing and output growth are bounded and checked before allocation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Match count, result count, output units, bytes, and execution work remain finite.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Results match ECMAScript code-unit behavior and can differ from Go regexp replacement conventions.
decisions.wire_consequences: Exact surrogate data requires a UTF-16-capable representation; ordinary Go-string output retains original byte slices where mapped.
decisions.upstream_status: Replacement and split requirements are mapped to the pinned ECMA-262 edition and differential surface.
decisions.reconsider_when: ECMA-262 changes substitution tokens or another output representation is added.
